name: New Relic
subcategory: uptime, errors, logs and status pages
tagline: Collect a small transparent telemetry stream and run a few dashboards locally

pricing.notes: Pricing is primarily usage based; canonical monthly amount is null.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 100 GB data ingest/month; 1 full-platform user; unlimited basic users; at least 8 days data retention; 500 synthetic checks/month
tiers.notes: Data above 100 GB and additional paid user types trigger charges.

tiers.name: Standard, core user
tiers.limits: Core observability access; unlimited basic users; Standard is limited to 5 full-platform users
tiers.notes: Data ingest is billed separately after the free allowance.

tiers.name: Standard, first full-platform user
tiers.limits: 1 discounted full-platform user; Standard supports up to 5 full-platform users

tiers.name: Standard, additional full-platform user
tiers.notes: The first full-platform user is separately priced at $10/month.

tiers.name: Pro, core user
tiers.limits: Core observability access with Pro plan controls

tiers.name: Pro, full-platform user
tiers.limits: Full-platform access with Pro controls and support
tiers.notes: $418.80/user on pay-as-you-go monthly billing or $349/user/month with annual commitment.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, ingest, support, retention and contract terms

pricing.freeTierCaps: 100 GB ingest/month; 1 full-platform user; unlimited basic users; 500 synthetic checks/month; minimum 8-day retention
pricing.billingTerms: Free; pay-as-you-go monthly + annual commitment options for Pro users; data ingest is usage billed
pricing.hiddenCosts: Original-data ingest above 100 GB is $0.40/GB or $0.60/GB for Data Plus; EU data region adds $0.05/GB, synthetic checks above allowance are $0.005/check, and extended retention/advanced compute add separate charges

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For New Relic, collect a small transparent telemetry stream and run a few dashboards locally. The hard boundary is large telemetry platform, agents, query engine, correlation, global ingestion, and support, plus independent infrastructure and reliable alerting.
coreLoopDIY: Collect a small transparent telemetry stream of bounded error and log events, run a few local dashboards, alert through one channel, and publish an honest status page.
requirements: server outside the monitored failure domain
whatYouLose: large telemetry platform, agents, query engine, correlation, global ingestion, and support
ongoingBurden: probe geography, clocks, retries, deduplication, sampling, storage, paging, notification delivery, on-call rules, and its own uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for New Relic because monitoring must continue working during the exact outage it reports, which makes independent infrastructure and alert delivery the real product. The recurring cost buys probe geography, clocks, retries, deduplication, sampling, storage, paging, notification delivery, on-call rules, and its own uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Uptime Kuma
priorArt.desc: Popular open-source uptime monitoring dashboard with many check types.

alternatives.name: Coroot
alternatives.desc: eBPF observability with opinions; best when your apps live in containers.

facts.install: Docker Compose for one host, or the Kubernetes Operator/Helm for a cluster
facts.engines: Core observability is non-AI; optional root-cause investigations connect to Coroot Cloud or configured Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
facts.dataFormat: Metrics use Prometheus-compatible storage or ClickHouse, while logs, traces, and profiles use ClickHouse; configuration uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL.
facts.gapVsPaid: Its automatic eBPF view is compelling for containers, but it lacks New Relic's broad language agents, browser and mobile monitoring, entity model, and managed integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: The eBPF node agent needs a supported Linux kernel and privileged host access on every node, and the product is most natural for containers and Kubernetes.

alternatives.name: HyperDX
alternatives.desc: Logs, traces, metrics, errors and replay in one ClickHouse-backed stack.

alternatives.name: OneUptime
alternatives.desc: Monitoring, incidents and status pages in one stack; simplicity did not survive.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or the release-branch Docker Compose stack; Helm is the production path
facts.engines: Its AI features can connect to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible servers such as vLLM, LocalAI, or LM Studio.
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted telemetry is stored in ClickHouse, application state and configuration in PostgreSQL, and cache, queues, and sessions in Redis.
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers a broad suite, but operating the stack is substantial work and its APM agents, entity correlations, and ecosystem are less mature than New Relic's.
facts.setupBlocker: The recommended self-hosted footprint is large and production requires secrets, TLS, backups, database care, and frequent upgrades rather than a single lightweight monitor.

alternatives.name: OpenObserve
alternatives.desc: A single-binary observability stack that remembers storage is not free.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or a single binary/Docker container; Helm plus external services for HA
facts.dataFormat: Telemetry is stored as Apache Parquet on local disk or object storage; single-node metadata defaults to SQLite, while HA uses PostgreSQL and NATS.
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles the core signals, but it lacks New Relic's mature application agents, browser and mobile telemetry, entity inventory, and managed-scale experience.
facts.setupBlocker: The easy single-node path still needs collectors and persistent storage; production HA adds Kubernetes, object storage, PostgreSQL, and NATS.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Uptime Kuma
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A good uptime dashboard, not a local telemetry, APM and log platform.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Data Plus plan and a small independent monitoring service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for New Relic in an empty repository.
Use Go, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, a Next.js 15 dashboard, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect a small transparent telemetry stream of bounded error and log events, run a few local dashboards, alert through one channel, and publish an honest status page.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement HTTP, TCP, DNS, TLS-expiry, and heartbeat checks with explicit timeout and retry policies.
Run checks from one independently hosted worker and store raw results plus incident state transitions.
Send deduplicated alerts to email or one webhook destination with recovery notifications.
Create services, maintenance windows, incidents, subscribers, and a public status page.
Add bounded event ingestion for application errors with sampling and sensitive-field scrubbing.
Provide health checks, retention settings, exports, backups, and a test-alert function.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a worldwide probe network.
Deliberately leave out phone, SMS, and managed on-call escalation.
Deliberately leave out unbounded logs, enterprise observability, and vendor-operated incident response.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
